newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Danish China rights resolution born of EU discord.
newsitem.headline: Danish China rights resolution born of EU discord.

text.p: Denmark said on Sunday it would introduce a resolution this week on China's human rights record at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva after discord thwarted attempts to agree a joint European Union motion.

Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen, taking part in a meeting of EU foreign ministers in the Netherlands, told reporters there was disagreement with France on the issue of whether such a motion should be put forward.
"They believe the time has run out for this kind of resolution. I disagree with that," Petersen told reporters. "There is a real disagreement, it is as simple as that."

"I regret the situation. I find it unfortunate," he said. "I would have much preferred that the EU this year as in previous years could agree on tabling a resolution on the human rights situation in China."
He said he believed the resolution would be introduced in Geneva on Thursday and that several countries would back it, including the United States and EU member Britain and some other EU countries.

The Netherlands, as holder of the rotating EU presidency, had been expected to present the annual EU-sponsored resolution on China on behalf of its 15 members with strong backing from the United States.

But France declared last week that dialogue with China was better than confrontation, and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, in a letter to his EU colleagues last week, said he understood three member states, who diplomats said were Germany, Spain and Italy, had taken a similar position.
Without these key member states on board, Van Mierlo suggested the Netherlands would not table a joint EU motion.
The United States and Britain both welcomed Denmark's decision and offered to co-sponsor the resolution.
"This decision by Denmark reflects its principled commitment to the universality of human rights," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement on Saturday.
In Geneva, diplomats said China had launched a rearguard action at the U.N. Human Rights Commission to head off the resolution condemning it for abusing human rights.
They said China was actively lobbying other countries to block the Danish resolution and that it might succeed again.
Every year since Beijing's bloody crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators in 1989, China has gathered enough support to block resolutions condemning its human rights record.
Petersen said he accepted that there had been some changes in China concerning its penal legislation. But, he added, "on other issues there has certainly been no progress".
"Therefore I disagree with the French assesment that what has happened in China should in any way lead to the fact that we should not table a resolution this year," he said.

The wording of the resolution had not yet been released but Petersen told the Danish news agency Ritzau that China should be criticised for its lack of respect for basic human rights such as freedom of assembly and speech.
Petersen added he hoped the Danish move would not harm its trade with China, where some of Denmark's biggest companies have extensive interests.
"It would be completely unreasonable if this were to have consequences for Denmark. If you cannot put foward criticism in this forum, where the devil can you do it," he told Ritzaus.
